body.working_title: TBATS in smooth: formulation, rationale and performance on the M4 hourly data

body.text: Is the TBATS of smooth, which places each trigonometric harmonic in the linear ARIMA slot of ADAM's state-space core as two states with lags 1 and 2, the same model as De Livera, Hyndman and Snyder's TBATS, and where does it differ from it by design?

How accurate are the point forecasts and the prediction intervals of smooth's TBATS on the M4 hourly series, against forecast::tbats, statsforecast's AutoTBATS, ADAM ETS and seasonal naive, and how long does it take?

body.definition: TBATS of the smooth package (R tbats(), Python TBATS), a linear single-source-of-error model in the Box-Cox space: y_t^(lambda) = w' v_{t-l} + e_t, v_t = F v_{t-l} + g e_t, with an ETS(A,N,N), ETS(A,A,N) or ETS(A,Ad,N) level and trend, and for each period m_i and harmonic j = 1..k_i (lambda_ij = 2 pi j / m_i) two states with lags 1 and 2 in the ARIMA slot of ADAM's core: u_t = v_{1,t-1} + v_{2,t-2}, v_{k,t} = eta_k u_t + g_k e_t with eta = (2 cos lambda_ij, -1) and g = (gamma_1i, sin(lambda_ij) gamma_2i - cos(lambda_ij) gamma_1i), so that (1 - 2 cos lambda_ij B + B^2) u_t = (g_1 B + g_2 B^2) e_t; an optional ADAM ARMA component (an additive state block, not ARMA errors); lambda in [0, 1] estimated by likelihood with the Jacobian; harmonics preselected by information criterion on a global OLS model of the Box-Cox series on Fourier terms; trend and ARMA orders selected by AICc.

TBATS of De Livera, Hyndman and Snyder (2011, JASA): y_t^(lambda) = l_{t-1} + phi b_{t-1} + sum_i sum_j s^(i)_{j,t-1} + d_t, l_t = l_{t-1} + phi b_{t-1} + alpha d_t, b_t = phi b_{t-1} + beta d_t, s^(i)_{j,t} = cos(lambda_ij) s^(i)_{j,t-1} + sin(lambda_ij) s*^(i)_{j,t-1} + gamma_1i d_t, s*^(i)_{j,t} = -sin(lambda_ij) s^(i)_{j,t-1} + cos(lambda_ij) s*^(i)_{j,t-1} + gamma_2i d_t, with ARMA(p, q) errors d_t = sum phi_k d_{t-k} + sum theta_k e_{t-k} + e_t.

The tbats() function of the R package forecast (Hyndman et al.), De Livera et al.'s TBATS with its own model selection, called with seasonal.periods = c(24, 168), single-threaded, otherwise default settings.
AutoTBATS of the Python package statsforecast (Nixtla), called with season_length = [24, 168], otherwise default settings.
ADAM ETS of smooth's Python port, ADAM(model='ZXZ', lags=[24, 168]) with its default settings: ETS with a daily and a weekly seasonal component selected by AICc.
Seasonal naive forecast repeating the last 168 observations (the last week) of the training sample.

The 414 hourly series of the M4 competition (Makridakis et al., 2020), training samples of 700 or 960 observations and test samples of 48, from the Mcompetitions/M4-methods repository (Dataset/Train/Hourly-train.csv, Dataset/Test/Hourly-test.csv).
The M4 hourly training samples with their last 48 observations held out as a validation test: fitting on observations 1..n-48 and evaluating on n-47..n; never the official test samples.
Each method is fitted once to each training sample and forecasts h = 1..48 steps ahead from its end; no refits, no rolling origin.
Mean absolute scaled error of a series: mean over h = 1..48 of |y_{n+h} - f_{n+h}| divided by the in-sample mean absolute seasonal difference at lag 24, as in M4.
Geometric mean over series of MASE(method A)/MASE(method B); below 1 means A is more accurate. Its 95% confidence interval is exp of the t-interval of the mean log ratio over series.
Share of the 414 x 48 test values inside the 95% prediction interval of a method.
Wall-clock seconds to fit a method to one training sample and produce its forecasts and intervals, single-threaded.

body.statement: With the same smoothing parameters, damping, Box-Cox lambda and initial states, [[TM1:smooth TBATS]] without ARMA gives the same one-step fitted values in the Box-Cox space as an independent implementation of [[TM2:De Livera TBATS]]'s rotation-form recursion, to a relative difference below 1e-8, for integer and fractional periods and with no, additive and damped trends.

body.statement: Backcasting through the harmonic block of [[TM1:smooth TBATS]] is exact: on a noise-free series made of a level and harmonics of a fractional period (7.3) and of an integer one (24), the fitted model with initial='backcasting' has in-sample errors below 1e-8 in absolute value.
body.question: Q1

body.statement: The ARMA of [[TM1:smooth TBATS]] is ADAM's additive ARMA component, not [[TM2:De Livera TBATS]]'s ARMA errors: for a level with smoothing parameter alpha and an AR(1) with coefficient phi, the impulse response of y to the innovation at lag j >= 1 is alpha + phi^j in smooth's model matrices, against phi^j + alpha (1 - phi^j)/(1 - phi) for ARMA errors.

body.text: The independent De Livera implementation reads smooth's initial Fourier coefficients one step later: smooth's coefficients (a, b) define s(t) = a sin(lambda t) + b cos(lambda t) with s(1) entering y_1, whereas De Livera's state s_0 enters y_1, so s_0 = a sin(lambda) + b cos(lambda) and s*_0 = a cos(lambda) - b sin(lambda). RN1 compared the recursions with s_0 = b (a time-origin mismatch of the initial states, not of the recursion); RN2 uses the conversion. The recursion equations of the independent implementation were not changed.
With the conversion, the fitted values agree to 1.7e-14 on the 72 exploratory cases of seeds 1 and 2; H2 and H3 checks behave as stated.
forecast::tbats is run from forecast 9.0.1 (the last release for R 4.3.3, the R that this container's apt provides; forecast 9.0.2 needs a newer R), with statsforecast 2.1.1 for AutoTBATS.
